clue.text: Resistance leader put gallon into family car, minutes before coppers arrived!

indicators.note: before puts the minutes ahead of the coppers in the answer
into says the gallon's letter goes inside the run made from family and car

parts.note: kin are one's family
taken as written
acta is Latin for records or minutes of proceedings
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so coppers are CUs

explanation.surface: A frantic motorist fills the family car with fuel, just before the police turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: KING CARACTACUS (Caratacus) led British resistance to the Roman invasion; he is also the king in the Rolf Harris song that 8 down spells out.
explanation.definitionFit: Caractacus was the British chieftain who fought the Romans, a leader of native resistance.

clue.text: Surcingle, say, with arms?

parts.note: a surcingle is a girth strap, but say it as 'Sir single': a lone knight of no order, entitled to a coat of arms

explanation.definitionFit: A knight bachelor is a knight belonging to no order of chivalry, the plainest 'Sir'.

clue.text: Land of song, say, in uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
eg (for example) is signalled by say
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country of song sees its people rise up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in uprising' turns the whole run AIR + EG + IN, giving NIGERIA; the second 'in' is part of the indicator, the first is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a country, and land is a common crossword word for a nation.

clue.text: Heart of glum reaper, going out with pantomime dame

indicators.note: going out says the reaper's letters sit outside the other piece

parts.note: a combine harvester reaps a crop

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, with the first and last letters dropped

explanation.surface: A gloomy Grim Reaper takes a pantomime dame out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbine is not a dame in the panto sense of a man in drag: she is the young heroine of the old harlequinade. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine is the sweetheart of Harlequin in the harlequinade that grew into British pantomime, a stock female role.

clue.text: The poet's sanguine horse, due for grooming

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A cheerful poet's horse is due to be brushed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for grooming' rearranges HORSE and DUE. 'The poet's' marks the hyphenated word as literary.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine can mean ruddy or rosy, and rose-hued is a poetic way of describing that colour.

clue.text: Conservative yes-man representing these islands

parts.note: split as yes and man: ay is an old word for yes, then man

explanation.surface: A Tory toady stands for a Caribbean island constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cayman Islands are a British territory in the Caribbean, so the name stands for these islands.

clue.text: A rider is below the apogee for one

parts.note: a rider is an addition, like a PS (postscript) added below a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cyclist sits beneath the highest point of an orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' is a link pointing the solver to the definition below the wordplay in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An apsis is either extreme point of an orbit; the apogee, farthest from Earth, is one example.

clue.text: You, say, lead attack on lecture

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud, you is the letter U
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A teacher leads an assault on someone's lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 'say' turns YOU into the single letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid is to scold or reprimand, much as to lecture someone does.

clue.text: Odalisques from "The Dames' Outing" (Rolf Harris). O, face the fact! Check out a disaster!

annotationWithheld.why: Odalisques = def; 'The Dames' Outing Rolf Harris O face the fact Check out a' anagrammed by 'disaster' gives this phrase plus KINGCARACTACUS (the 1-across answer), which no word of this clue supplies, so the composite cannot be written with clue words.
annotationWithheld.clue: Odalisques from "The Dames' Outing" (Rolf Harris). O, face the fact! Check out a disaster!

clue.text: Legends of Barham's body sling manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres moves the letters about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stories of a strongman's sling being manoeuvred into place.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Barham wrote 'The Ingoldsby Legends' under the pen name Thomas Ingoldsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Barham's comic verse tales are known as the Ingoldsby Legends, after his pseudonym.

clue.text: Malaysian state banning telecom operators from Sunday

indicators.note: banning means these letters are kept out of the other word

parts.note: the Christian Sabbath is Sunday
BT is the British telecom company

explanation.surface: A Malaysian state bars phone companies from operating on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B and T from SABBATH leaves SABAH; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabah is one of Malaysia's states, in the north of Borneo.

clue.text: See 8
Some tack, lead and play for time

parts.note: to head something is to lead it
to stall is to delay or play for time

explanation.surface: An actor leads the cast but stalls for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstall is the part of a bridle round a horse's head, one item of riding tack.

clue.text: Like 1 across, she resisted a gamble in fine feathers

indicators.note: in says the other pieces are placed inside the feathers

parts.note: a boa is a feathery scarf
to dice is to gamble

explanation.surface: A woman wrapped in a feather boa refuses to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: BOADICEA (Boudicca) led a British revolt against Rome, like Caractacus.
explanation.definitionFit: Boadicea was the Iceni queen who rose against Roman rule, a female resistance leader.

clue.text: Stayed in the arms of Morpheus, enfolding Psyche

indicators.note: enfolding means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Morpheus is the god of dreams, so in his arms is asleep, abed
the id is part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: Someone lingered asleep, dreaming of the goddess Psyche.
explanation.definitionFit: Abided is a past tense of abide, to remain or stay.

clue.text: No rabbi cooked game for this Irish icon

indicators.note: cooked as in tampered with, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A rabbi refuses to cook game for an Irish hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Boru was a High King of Ireland and a national hero.

clue.text: John Peel's portfolio? Or the folio?

definitions.meaning: the radio disc jockey's stock of records to air
Shakespeare's First Folio is a collected list of his plays

explanation.surface: A huntsman's case of papers, or perhaps a printed volume.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a famed BBC radio DJ, not the huntsman of the song.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlist is a DJ's set of records, and the Folio is literally a list of plays.

clue.text: A dog? According to him it is!

definitions.meaning: Edward ... wrote an arithmetic book, hence 'according to ...' meaning correct

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a certain animal really is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocker is a spaniel, and 'according to Cocker' is an old idiom for something right.

clue.text: See 8
English and American cities adopt secure backing of union

indicators.note: backing means the whole construction is read from right to left
adopt says the cities take in the other piece

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, LA is Los Angeles
to nail is to secure

explanation.surface: English and American towns twin to bolster a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopt' places NAIL between EC and LA; 'backing' turns ECNAILLA into ALLIANCE. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: How kippers are caught?

parts.note: kippers here are people having a kip, a sleep, rather than smoked herrings

explanation.definitionFit: To be caught napping is to be taken unawares, as dozing sleepers would be.

clue.text: Capital! When mother ran off with knight

parts.note: as can mean when
ma is mother

indicators.note: off with means the knight is carried away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: An exclamation that mother has eloped with a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of delight, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asmara is the capital city of Eritrea.

clue.text: How one competes with lousy mule spinning

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: A contestant races against a spinning mule.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulously means in a spirit of rivalry, trying to equal or excel others.

clue.text: See 8
Tommy's done for, Bonaparte's half-cut: nothing for it!

indicators.note: half-cut means the name is cut in half, keeping only the first half

parts.note: Napoleon was Bonaparte's first name
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier is finished, Napoleon is drunk, and nothing can be done.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a British private soldier; NAPOO was First World War slang for finished. 'for it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoo, from French 'il n'y en a plus', meant finished or dead in Tommy's slang.

clue.text: Just sober chamber ensemble?

parts.note: 'one over the eight' means drunk, so being just sober is merely the eight itself

explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight musicians playing chamber music.

clue.text: Panic on isthmus, some worshipper abjuring images

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Alarm breaks out on a narrow strip of land among iconoclastic believers.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniconist rejects the use of images or idols in worship.

clue.text: Postwar regulars get fat, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: After the war, the pub regulars sadly put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is a struggle, so post-war means after one.
